evals.name: coupon-expiry
evals.prompt: Turn this PO requirement into a spec with acceptance criteria and a test plan: "Coupons should be able to expire. A coupon gets an optional expiry date. Applying an expired coupon to a cart must fail with a clear message, and the coupon lookup must not return an expired coupon as valid."
evals.expected_output: specs/<slug>/ with spec.md, acceptance-criteria.md (Given/when/then ACs) and test-plan.md mapping every AC; the Specs lint passes.
expectations: An acceptance criterion covers rejecting an expired coupon with a clear message
An acceptance criterion covers a coupon without an expiry date continuing to work
The test plan maps every acceptance criterion to a test layer

evals.name: order-cancellation-window
evals.prompt: Turn this PO requirement into a spec with acceptance criteria and a test plan: "Customers can cancel an order within 30 minutes of placing it, unless the payment has already been captured. Cancelling releases the reserved stock."
evals.expected_output: specs/<slug>/ with testable ACs for the 30-minute window, the captured-payment rejection and the stock release; the Specs lint passes.
expectations: Acceptance criteria cover both sides of the 30-minute boundary
An acceptance criterion covers rejecting cancellation once payment is captured
An acceptance criterion covers releasing the reserved stock on cancellation

evals.name: ambiguous-requirement
evals.prompt: Turn this PO requirement into a spec with acceptance criteria and a test plan: "Make checkout faster for returning customers."
evals.expected_output: Surfaces open questions (what faster means, which steps, how returning customers are identified) instead of inventing specifics.
expectations: Lists concrete open questions, such as what 'faster' means, which checkout steps change, and how a returning customer is identified
Does not invent acceptance criteria for points the requirement leaves undecided; any spec it writes puts them under Open questions
